thread:
noah: FYI canary p99 host CPU up ~2.4x on short-stream workload this morning, noticed higher small-write churn
sana: any traces? where's the hotspot?
leo: uploaded perf bundle: https://perf.internal/r/rv-1869994321 (internal) - sampled stacks look host-heavy
noah: quick breakdown from sampled flame: token_normalize -> rust_ingress_shim -> grpc::writev -> header::parse -> kvcache::evict_check
anya: header::parse + writev indicates HPACK inflation and many tiny frames; smallwrite_ratio is through the roof
leo: we pushed a kernel-scorer change yesterday that prefers int4/int8 short-seq kernels when batch<3 to save GPU cycles
sana: that scorer tweak was supposed to help throughput, not blow up host tail though
noah: local repro with ingress harness: enable scorer=v-shortbind + streaming chunking -> small-write count + writev latency both double; host p99 jumps accordingly
leo: repro steps I used:
```
1) load canary token histogram (p50/p95) into harness
2) enable streaming framing + scorer=v-shortbind
3) run 60s capture with perf-map + grpc tracing
4) collect flame and tcp packets
```
devops-bot: Regression alert: host_cpu_p99 increased 136% on canary @2026-03-23T18:12Z (trace rv-1869994321)
anya: also noticed kvcache evict_check rising - I think fragmentation increased the number of short-lived KV entries and eviction loops fire more often
sana: TL;DR: GPU-side win for int kernels but increases host fragmentation -> net worse tail on canary
leo: short-term mitigations proposed: 1) revert scorer change on canary 2) throttle kvcache eviction background loop 3) enable a micro-coalesce write heuristic for grpc to coalesce adjacent small writes within 400us window
noah: rolled revert + canary-only micro-coalesce flag + kvcache throttle; p99 dropped back toward baseline within 8 minutes
perf-bot: Regression alert closed after revert @2026-03-23T18:24Z
anya: micro-coalesce helped in local runs but we need to avoid increased latency for large bursts; heuristic must be adaptive (window shrink if backlog forms)
sana: longer-term: extend kernel selector cost model to include a host_frag_cost (host_penalty) term. current scoring is GPU-centric and misses host IO/parse costs
leo: proposal for host_frag_cost modeling: simulate per-request fragmentation given selector choice, estimate small_write_ratio, header_parse_cycles, and expected kvcache churn; aggregate into a penalty coefficient added to selector score
noah: I'll open INF-4921 to track: host_frag_cost, micro-coalesce flag, and kvcache tuning. assigning to leo/anya
anya: also: add observability meters - small_write_ratio, avg_writev_latency, header_parse_cpu_pct, kvcache_eviction_rate - so future scorer rollouts can be evaluated against host metrics
sana: schedule: leo will deliver a simulator + unit tests, anya will add metrics, noah will own the canary validation and postmortem if revert holds
leo: small note - simulator should replay realistic byte-aligned chunking (HPACK effects matter) not just token counts; we need to model header compression inflation under many small frames
anya: agreed. I'll capture HPACK expansion samples from the perf bundle and add to the sim corpus
noah: next steps: keep revert on canary until host_penalty patch lands; run an A/B with micro-coalesce enabled vs disabled; if stable, we'll do a short postmortem and mark the scorer rollout blocked
sana: good triage. please attach flamegraphs and trace bundle to INF-4921. thanks all :eyes:
